notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

New ports in Ports and Apps, each made from your own copy of the game. Upload the game on the
web page (a disc image, or a .zip or .7z holding one); the console sets it up once and the
tile plays it.

The Jak games: Jak and Daxter, Jak II and Jak 3 run natively through OpenGOAL from your PS2
discs. The console sets each one up once from your disc, in 1 to 5 minutes, at the upload or
on the first Play. Jak and Daxter holds 60 fps; Jak II 54 to 60; Jak 3 58 to 60, with a few
heavy scenes at 52 to 57.

Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus runs natively through ProjectCane, with its author's
permission, at 60 fps from your USA PS2 disc. The first setup takes about a minute from an
ISO and about three from a CHD.

The Wind Waker (GameCube) runs natively through SwitchWaker at 30 fps, full speed, from your
USA GameCube disc in the GameCube library.

Super Smash Bros. Melee runs natively through melee-pc from your USA 1.02 disc in the
GameCube library, at 60 fps in testing. Its project's own release is downloaded (20 MB) when
you tick it in Add ports and apps. Its shaders build in the background for about three
minutes the first time.

LEGO Island runs natively through isle-portable at 60 fps from your LEGO Island CD image, any
version or language.

PokeMMO: the tile downloads the official client on its first launch. You need a PokeMMO
account and your own games: Pokemon Black or White, plus FireRed, Emerald, Platinum and
HeartGold or SoulSilver if you have them. Games in your library are passed to it at each
start.

YouTube (VacuumTube) and Stremio are new app tiles in Add ports and apps, installed from
Flathub on their first launch. The controller works them like a keyboard: the bottom button
selects and the right button goes back.

Moonlight now uses Switchroot's own build, which decodes the stream with the Switch's video
hardware. It installs on the tile's first launch (a small package), and the PCs you paired
before carry over. For Moonlight away from home, the web page's new Accounts tab can sign the
console in to Tailscale.

Wind Waker HD builds from a disc image now: a .wux or .wud with its disc key, as well as a
.wua archive or a game folder. A build from a disc image also needs the Wii U common key:
type it, or choose the otp.bin from your Wii U dump, which holds it. It is used for that
build only and not saved. A first build takes about 20 minutes instead of 38. Prepare
graphics now starts once you are in a game, tries a place that failed once more, and keeps
its minutes left across restarts. On the web page, Rebuild now gets the update (about 20
minutes, plugged in; later rebuilds reuse it and take seconds). Mario Kart Wii's first build
takes about 37 minutes instead of 45. Game setups and builds now take turns, one at a time.

Deep sleep on the original Switch with the extreme overclock no longer hangs on wake. The fix
is in the boot files, so it works after this update's second restart; until then that
console keeps turning only the screen off. On the charger, deep sleep now wakes only for a
press of the power button. Turning the screen off now disconnects Bluetooth controllers after
a minute whether deep sleep is on or off.

The RAM and CPU tuners refuse to start on a charger under 12 W, like a computer's USB port,
and say why: a run draws about 10 W for hours, so a weaker charger let the battery run flat
in the middle of it. An original Switch installed fresh could have its CPU limit saved above
what the model reaches; it is reset to the model's maximum.

A Game language row is now in the pre-launch menu for PS2, Saturn and 3DS games too. On
GameCube and Wii the row only ever applied the first language chosen, and a game's settings
file, with its cheats, could be saved empty; both are fixed. On PSP the row had no effect;
fixed.

Wii U games with no shader cache of their own get the community's cache, so they stutter
less the first time they are played. Halo and Jak II skip a display layer they do not need:
Halo's menu went from 54 to 60 fps. Plugging headphones into the console's jack switches the
sound to them in handheld. The web page is split into tabs: Files, Graphics, Accounts, PC
Games/Apps, Update, Contributions and Debug. ROM folders named the way other frontends name
them (PS2 Games, Nintendo 64, GBA ROMs) are found. The Debug bundle includes the reason for
the console's last power-off. The SCCM Retro app no longer says it needs WiFi when the card
holds a setup kit.

Not yet tested: Melee docked or online; the Jak games' PAL, Japanese and Korean discs (only
USA discs were tried), and Jak 3's catacomb rail ride on a long run, where memory is tight;
logging in to PokeMMO; a real Moonlight stream with the new decoder; signed-in YouTube
playback and Stremio playback; the new ports docked; deep sleep on an original Switch with a
press of the power button to wake it.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
